claim: The ISM Services Supplier Deliveries Index hit 56.8% in April — 3.9 pp above its 12-month average — and the ongoing Strait of Hormuz closure is likely to keep delivery times stretched in May, mechanically supporting the composite index (slower deliveries count as expansionary in ISM methodology).
source_name: Institute for Supply Management via PR Newswire

claim: Wood Mackenzie warned on May 20 that the Hormuz closure 'risks the greatest global energy supply shock in decades,' with oil potentially hitting $200/bbl — prolonged disruption would keep Supplier Deliveries and Prices sub-indices at elevated readings that inflate the ISM composite.

The ISM Business Activity sub-index surged to 55.9% in April (up 2 pp from March), and the Backlog of Orders held in expansion at 53% for a third straight month — well above its 12-month average of 46.4% — indicating a pipeline of demand that could sustain headline activity into May.
source_name: Institute for Supply Management via PR Newswire

claim: The ISM Services 12-month average has risen four consecutive months (from 51.7% in December 2025 to 52.5% in April), reflecting a broadening uptrend in services activity that provides upward momentum for May.
source_name: Institute for Supply Management via PR Newswire

claim: The S&P Global Flash US Services PMI fell to 50.9 in May (vs 51.0 prior and 51.2 estimate), with S&P Global explicitly noting services are 'on course for its weakest calendar quarter since late 2023' and new business inflows rose only modestly — this is the strongest concurrent leading indicator available and points to deceleration.

The Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index dipped to 93.1 in May (from 93.8 revised), with the Present Situation Index dropping 3.2 points to 121.2 and two-thirds of consumers cutting back on spending — softening demand is a direct headwind to services activity.
source_name: The Conference Board via PR Newswire

claim: The ISM Services Employment Index was 48% in April — its second consecutive month of contraction — signaling ongoing labor market weakness in services that would weigh on output and new business.
source_name: Institute for Supply Management via PR Newswire

claim: The ISM New Orders Index plunged 7.1 pp in April to 53.5%, suggesting the pre-price-shock order pull-forward in March was a one-off; any further normalization of new orders in May would drag the headline lower.
source_name: Institute for Supply Management via PR Newswire

claim: The ISM April report noted that Retail Trade was one of only three contracting industries, and a May 26 survey found two-thirds of Americans are cutting back spending amid Middle East fuel price shocks — consumer-facing services face a direct demand headwind into May.
